fomc-2026-10.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-10.recent: Gasoline pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, mid-way through a hiking cycle, and Trump allies have urged no hike before the midterms a week later. Warsh has withheld guidance and called AI a shock to the economy; this meeting shows how his committee weighs oil-driven prices against that political pressure.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-10.recent: Households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, while the ECB's own survey finds loan obstacles hitting 7% of firms, which leaves the council between expectations drifting up and credit already tightening. Lagarde has credited the bond selloff in France with doing some of that tightening, and the argument is whether it buys time before December.

boj-2026-10.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-10.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, and the question in Tokyo is whether wage gains now drive inflation on their own, which is what would justify further tightening. The Board decides while the yen still funds the Latin American carry trade through a Brazil rout, so its move reaches well past Japan.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-11.recent: This decision lands as inflation and borrowing data set out the chancellor's Budget challenge, so the committee weighs price pressure while fiscal policy is still unsettled. It also meets during an energy shock, with Iran threats hanging over oil, and whether to hike into such a shock is the argument in front of it.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: This is the first meeting after the midterms, which Trump allies wanted kept free of a hike. Gasoline pushed US inflation to 3.7% in September, TD Securities expected 3 dissents against the October hold, and Warsh, who calls AI a shock to the economy, has withheld guidance on whether rate hikes resume.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The Miami summit opens with its guest list in dispute: Merz has urged Trump to invite South Africa. Zelenskyy is eyeing a meeting with the US and Russia on its margins, as Putin pushes a three-way summit with Trump and Xi. And the Emissions Gap Report has just named the United States the G20's outlier on climate.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro-area households now expect 3.1% inflation, up from 3%, while the ECB's own survey finds 7% of firms hitting obstacles to bank loans. That is December's bind: whether to answer rising expectations by raising rates on firms already short of credit, with France's bond rout showing how fast borrowing costs spread across the bloc.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: The committee decides after inflation and borrowing data that sharpened the chancellor's Budget challenge, so its call lands on a government with little room. With Iran threats keeping oil in play, it faces the question now argued openly: whether to hike rates in an energy shock or look through it.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: The board's question is whether Japan's inflation is now driven by wages or is still imported: yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago. Its answer reaches beyond Japan, to a Latin American carry trade funded in yen that held through the Brazil rout.

fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's monthly report on personal income and spending, carrying the PCE price index the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. It moves rate expectations, Treasury yields and the dollar.
fred-us-pce-2026-10-29.recent: The Bureau of Economic Analysis releases the latest US PCE figures, which settle how fast the prices American households pay are rising and whether their spending is keeping pace with their income.

fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's quarterly estimate of US gross domestic product, first published about a month after each quarter ends and revised twice after. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed expectations move on it.
fred-us-gdp-2026-10-29.recent: It lands in the week the Fed is set to lead a G7 trio in a hawkish rate pause, so the first read of the quarter's output reaches officials as they decide whether holding still fits the economy. After the IMF upgraded its 2026 growth forecast and warned of a split outlook, it shows which side of that split the US sits on.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly employment report, released on the first Friday of most months, counting jobs added, the unemployment rate and wage growth. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets reprice within minutes.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-11-06.recent: This release reports a month of payroll hiring, the unemployment rate and average hourly pay, along with revisions to the two months before it. It settles how much the labor market added or shed over that month, the reading rate-setters weigh against inflation.
